name: Pulping Golem

source.title: Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale

items.name: Golem Antimagic
items.text:
Harmed by acid (6d10+4 untyped, 2d8+4 untyped from areas and persistent damage); healed by fire (area 2d8+4 healing HP); slowed by electricity

---

items.name: Vulnerable to Neutralize Poison
items.text: Casting Cleanse Affliction on the golem deactivates its Breath Weapon for 1 minute.

items.name: Vulnerable to Rust
items.text: Magical rusting effects, like a rust monster's antennae, affect the iron golem normally.

items.name: Breath Weapon
items.text:
The pulping golem spills its cauldron stomach to the floor, dealing 9d12 fire damage to creatures within 10 feet (DC 33 basic Reflex save save).

It can't use Breath Weapon again for 1d4 rounds.

items.name: Extend Legs
items.text: The pulping golem extends its legs up to a height of 40 feet, raising its body high into the air. While its legs are extended, its movement speed is halved, and it takes a -2 penalty to its Fortitude save DC against Shove and Trip attempts.

items.name: Inexorable March
items.text: The iron golem Strides up to its Speed, pushing back each creature whose space it moves into and damaging them if they try to stop its movement. A creature can attempt to bar the way by succeeding at a DC 39 Fortitude save save. On a critical success, the resisting creature takes no damage; otherwise, it is damaged as if hit by the golem's fist.

items.name: Iron Golem Poison
items.text:
Any Drained value from this poison is reduced by 1 every hour.

Saving Throw DC 35 Fortitude save

---

Maximum Duration 4 rounds

Stage 1 2d6+4 poison damage and Drained 1 (1 round)

Stage 2 4d6+4 poison damage and Drained 2 (1 round)

Stage 3 8d6+4 poison damage and Drained 3 (1 round)

text: Traditionally crafted into the forms of giant suits of armor or powerful animals, iron golems are products of exquisite artistry and skill. Their articulated joints and sturdy armored bodies require great care and mathematical precision to craft, and regular cleaning and oiling ensure they don't rust over the ages. With proper care, iron golems can remain in good shape for thousands of years, being passed down for generations, as long as they aren't destroyed by meddlesome adventurers. In addition to their incredible strength, iron golems possess a potent toxic breath weapon that is often more than enough to dispatch entire groups of opponents.
